name: Proto-Elamite
sign_inventory: ~1,200 signs after Dahl's collation (earlier raw list ~1,900); >1,600 texts; ~1,050 signs occur once
contact_evidence_with_indus: none direct (predates Mature Harappan c. 2600-1900 BCE)
claimed_link_to_indus: none verified this session; comparandum for short administrative texts, numeracy and sign-list method
label: n/a (typological comparandum)

name: Linear Elamite
script_type: claimed largely phonographic (Desset et al.); Maeder: ~70% phonetic + logograms
sign_inventory: Desset et al. claim readings for 72 signs (>96% of known); small corpus
contact_evidence_with_indus: contemporary neighbour of Indus; no Indus-Elamite bilingual known
claimed_link_to_indus: methodological model: decipherment from royal names on Elamite cuneiform/Linear Elamite parallel objects (silver beakers)
label: decipherment = contested but substantially supported (Krebernik/Stolper/Steinkeller positive; Maeder sceptical; criticism re unprovenanced beakers)

name: Konar Sandal 'Geometric' script
sign_inventory: small (4 tablets; 3 bigraphic with Linear Elamite)
contact_evidence_with_indus: regional (Jiroft culture interacted with Indus world per Laursen 2016 context)
claimed_link_to_indus: Madjidzadeh proposed evolution into Linear Elamite (rejected by Desset 2014); no Indus link established
label: speculative (any Indus link)

name: Mesopotamian cuneiform (Sumerian/Akkadian)
sign_inventory: several hundred signs in use per period (not quantified this session)
contact_evidence_with_indus: Meluhha named in texts; Shu-ilishu seal AO 22310 ('eme-bal me-luh-ha' = interpreter of Meluhha; Louvre: Akkad 2340-2200 BCE; CDLI: Ur III); Indus-style seals found in Mesopotamia (Penn MAIS)
claimed_link_to_indus: Meluhha = Indus region; best hope for a bilingual
label: established (trade contact); Meluhha=Indus identification widely accepted (inference from goods/geography)

name: Gulf / Dilmun seals (Bahrain; Failaka)
dates: c. 2100-2000 BCE ('Gulf Type'); Dilmun Type thereafter
script_type: Indus-character inscriptions on Gulf Type seals; later Dilmun glyptic
contact_evidence_with_indus: Gulf Type seals with Indus signs; Indus cubical weights at Bahrain; Dilmun weight standard based on Indus unit (c. 2050 BC); Indus sherds with graffiti at Qala'at al-Bahrain
claimed_link_to_indus: abnormal frequency of prefixed 'twins' sign suggests a non-Harappan language/local convention (Laursen; Parpola 1994)
label: established (contact); plausible (different-language hypothesis)

name: Magan (Oman peninsula; Umm an-Nar)
contact_evidence_with_indus: listed among polities that disintegrated with Indus decline (Laursen 2016); specific Indus finds not verified this session
label: plausible (not checked in detail)

name: Oxus civilisation / BMAC
script_type: no script established (one potsherd-signs paper: Klochkov 1999)
contact_evidence_with_indus: Indus elephant seal with Indus signs at Gonur Depe; two provincial Indus seals at Altyn Depe; Indus outpost at Shortughai; ivory; BMAC material in Baluchistan/Indus
label: established (contact)

name: Egyptian hieroglyphs
claimed_link_to_indus: typological comparandum only (decipherment via bilingual + names)
label: n/a

name: Southern Neolithic / Megalithic graffiti marks; Sembiyan-Kandiyur celt
dates: celt: Mahadevan's broad date c. 2000-1000 BCE; graffiti mostly Iron Age/Early Historic (many undated)
sign_inventory: 42 base signs, 544 variants, 1,521 composites (Rajan & Sivanantham via harappa.com); 13,702 potsherds documented (TN policy note)
contact_evidence_with_indus: Mahadevan: four Indus signs on stone celt; Indus-like 'muruku' symbol on megalithic pottery
claimed_link_to_indus: continuity of Indus signs in South India
label: speculative (context/dating problems; resemblance of simple marks)

name: Brahmi / Tamil-Brahmi
dates: Mauryan period onward (3rd c. BCE; Tamil-Brahmi early dates debated)
claimed_link_to_indus: Hunter 1934 proposed Indus derivation; Yajnadevam claims Brahmi = standardized Indus signs
label: Indus->Brahmi: speculative (Salomon: 'premature'); Aramaic-derivation favoured but unresolved

name: Rongorongo
claimed_link_to_indus: Hevesy 1932: visual resemblance to Indus signs
label: refuted (Metraux 1938 rebuttal; chronology)
